The nuts and dry fruits industry value chain encompasses a series of interconnected activities, ranging from agricultural production to end consumption. Each stage contributes to value addition, quality differentiation, cost structure and margin profile, and is influenced by factors such as agro-climatic conditions, technological adoption, scale of operations, regulatory compliance and market demand. 1. Cultivation & Procurement The value chain begins with cultivation and procurement. In India, domestic production supports crops such as groundnuts and certain dry fruits, including raisins. …

The Indian nuts and dry fruits market, is estimated at approximately USD 25444 Million in FY 2025, is projected to reach USD 36055 Million by FY 2030, reflecting a CAGR of 7.22 percent, driven by shifts in dietary habits, premiumisation, rapid urbanisation, and the deepening penetration of e-commerce, quick-commerce, and modern retail platforms. Domestic consumption is expanding across both mass-market and premium categories. Groundnuts continue to dominate in volume terms due to their affordability, availability, and use across oil extraction, snacks, and traditional foods. …

The non-premium segment accounted for approximately 70% of the total market value in FY 2025, with an estimated market size of USD 17,811 million. This segment primarily comprises loose, unbranded or minimally processed products distributed through traditional retail formats, mandis, and local wholesalers. Consumption in this segment is largely price-driven and concentrated in mass-market categories such as groundnuts, loose raisins, dates, and economy-grade nuts, which are extensively used for household consumption, oil extraction, traditional sweets, and food processing applications. …

Within the dry fruits segment, dates constitute the largest category, accounting for approximately 39.79% of the segment value, with an estimated market size of USD 939.96 million. Dates benefit from widespread household consumption, use as a natural sweetener, and strong seasonal demand during festive and religious periods, supporting both retail and institutional consumption. From a product-form perspective, the dates market is commonly segmented into wet dates and dry dates, based on moisture content, shelf life, and consumption patterns. …

India’s nuts and dry fruits trade reflects a structurally differentiated pattern across product categories, with a pronounced import dependence in certain segments and a strong export orientation in others. Over the period from 2021 to 2025, total imports of nuts and dry fruits increased from USD 2,684.41 million to USD 3,777.59 million, while exports fluctuated within a narrower range, from USD 1,185.97 million in FY 2021 to USD 1,175.42 million in FY 2025. This trend indicates a widening trade deficit for the category, primarily driven by rising imports. …

Upon receipt of the PR, the procurement team undertakes vendor sourcing from the domestic market. Price quotations are obtained and evaluated to ensure cost efficiency, transparent commercial terms, and timely supply. 3. …

Goods are delivered directly by the domestic suppliers to the Company’s warehouse or to a designated third-party location, as applicable. The supplier is required to provide relevant commercial documents such as the tax invoice, delivery challan, and any applicable quality or compliance certifications. 5.

Upon receipt of goods, a Goods Receipt Note (GRN) is generated after verification of quantity and preliminary quality checks by the Company’s team. Detailed quality inspection is carried out to ensure conformity with specifications. Any discrepancies in quantity or quality are documented through a Non-Conformance Report (NCR) and communicated to the vendor for corrective action. Red Herring Prospectus 196 | P a g e 6.

The Finance team processes payments based on a three-way matching of the Purchase Order, GRN, and supplier invoice. Payments to domestic vendors are made through banking channels such as NEFT or RTGS, in accordance with the agreed credit terms. 7.

All procurement-related documents, including PRs, POs, GRNs, invoices, and payment records, are systematically maintained in the Company’s accounting and record-keeping systems to ensure audit readiness and traceability. Periodic reviews are conducted to assess vendor performance, monitor procurement costs, and ensure adherence to delivery timelines, supporting operational efficiency and risk management. Import Procurement Process 1. Vendor Identification The Company sources dry fruits from overseas suppliers located in key producing regions. …

Almonds are procured in in-shell form from approved suppliers. Upon receipt, the material undergoes inspection for moisture content, infestation, shell integrity, and overall quality. Accepted lots are stored in clean, dry, and ventilated storage areas.

The in-shell almonds are fed into almond cracking machines where controlled mechanical pressure is applied to crack the shell without damaging the kernel. Post-cracking, a sorting and separation machine segregates kernels from shells based on size, weight, and airflow.

After machine separation, kernels are transferred to sorting tables where manual workers inspect and segregate almonds based on size and appearance, broken or damaged kernels, and foreign matter. Rejected material is separated, and only acceptable kernels proceed to packing. Quality Control & Inspection Red Herring Prospectus 198 | P a g e Quality control checks are conducted at various stages of the processing cycle to ensure conformity with internal standards and customer specifications. …

Finished almond products are packed using a combination of semi-automatic and manual packing methods into different pack sizes as per the order received. Each pack is sealed, labeled, and batch-coded as per regulatory and customer requirements. Processing of Walnuts
Walnuts are procured in in-shell form and inspected for shell condition, kernel quality, moisture, and infestation. Accepted lots are stored under hygienic conditions
Walnuts are cracked entirely by manual labor using hand tools. Due to the delicate nature of walnut kernels, mechanical cracking is avoided to prevent excessive breakage

After cracking, workers manually extract kernels and sort them based on size and color, whole versus broken kernels, and visual quality and cleanliness. Shell fragments and rejected kernels are removed at this stage

The extracted kernels undergo further manual grading to meet customer-specific quality specifications. Quality control checks are conducted to ensure conformity with internal quality standards relating to appearance, cleanliness, moisture and absence of defects. Only kernels that meet the prescribed quality parameters are approved for packing.

Walnut kernels are packed manually into different pack sizes as per the orders received.
